scope: All rows in the bounded saved IDL join; unreviewed includes absent and unobserved names. Classifications and WPT links are manually selected review leads, not mediation tests or safety judgments.

beacon.why: Native sendBeacon behavior and server receipt; adapt as a control rather than treating it as a runtime test.

fetch-later.why: Examples of deferred request behavior; existing project probe separately measures page-close delivery.

navigation-preload.why: Exercises the native navigation-preload API; application access and browser state still need separate analysis.

fedcm.why: Example of FedCM requests that the service worker does not observe; it does not establish publisher access to a seeded runtime identity.

cache-add.why: Cache.add/addAll behavior in Window and worker; not a test of runtime interception.

background-fetch-upload.why: Tests background fetch with request uploads; related fixtures and browser support are still required.

fedcm-userinfo.why: FedCM getUserInfo scenarios; does not establish the relevant state is reachable in the deployed runtime.

preload-headers.why: Navigation preload request-header behavior; not a test of app access to native registration.

websocket-close.why: WebSocket close reason behavior; the pinned case is not a runtime confinement test.

websocket-send.why: Native WebSocket send behavior; it does not by itself calibrate application-secret delivery.

webtransport-connect.why: Connection setup examples in Window and worker; the test and its server dependencies are not executed here.

serviceworker-register.why: Native service worker registration and default scope behavior; does not test runtime virtualization.

rows.effect: Constructs a synthetic background-fetch event.
rows.prerequisites: Requires constructor exposure and valid init; synthetic events are not necessarily trusted or active.
rows.next: Distinguish browser-created events and their registration authority from synthetic objects.

rows.effect: Exposes the registration associated with a background-fetch event.
rows.prerequisites: Requires an accessible event with an associated registration.
rows.next: Determine native event provenance and test subsequent record access and abort authority.

rows.effect: Schedules background requests and can include request bodies; requests can outlive the initiating page.
rows.prerequisites: Requires a native registration with an active worker and permission not denied; the draft rejects no-cors requests.
rows.next: Determine native registration reachability in prepared workers and test upload receiver and lifecycle behavior; earlier probe used seeded registration and a download.

rows.effect: Returns a registration for an existing background fetch identified by id, or null.

rows.effect: Returns ids of existing background fetches associated with the registration.

rows.effect: Returns a readable stream yielding server-initiated bidirectional streams with both readable and writable sides.
rows.prerequisites: Requires access to a WebTransport object and server-created streams in a live session.
rows.next: Test acquisition of an incoming stream and its writable side with a receiver; reading this property alone sends no payload.

rows.effect: Returns a readable stream of server-initiated receive streams.
rows.prerequisites: Requires an accessible session and incoming streams.
rows.next: Assess how received bytes become available; a separate writable capability is needed to transmit.

rows.effect: Returns the transport negotiated application protocol.
rows.prerequisites: Requires a reachable native WebTransport object; browser support and connection state can affect values.
rows.next: Assess native session acquisition and other stream or datagram capabilities independently; a getter is not a payload send.

rows.effect: Returns a promise for session readiness.
rows.prerequisites: Requires an accessible WebTransport object and relevant state changes.
rows.next: Examine associated callbacks and peer-provided data; the getter does not itself establish a payload transfer.

rows.effect: Returns the transport transport reliability mode.
rows.prerequisites: Requires a reachable native WebTransport object; browser support and connection state can affect values.
rows.next: Assess native session acquisition and other stream or datagram capabilities independently; a getter is not a payload send.

rows.effect: Exposes the response headers of an established WebTransport session, initially null.
rows.prerequisites: Requires a reachable native WebTransport object and successful session setup to obtain server response headers.
rows.next: Check header exposure and downstream relay in actual browsers; a getter does not itself establish a new connection.

rows.effect: Static feature query reports whether exclusively reliable sessions are supported.
rows.prerequisites: Requires an exposed native WebTransport constructor and implementation of the static property; the snapshot did not observe it.
rows.next: Measure browser availability and any effects of feature detection; do not infer support or a network request from the pinned IDL declaration.

rows.effect: Returns the readable stream of a bidirectional transport stream.
rows.prerequisites: Requires a reachable bidirectional stream object and appropriate transport state.
rows.next: Test actual reads and subsequent uses; obtaining the property is not itself payload transmission.

rows.effect: Returns the writable stream of a bidirectional transport stream.
rows.prerequisites: Requires a reachable bidirectional stream object and appropriate transport state.
rows.next: Test actual writes at an independent receiver; obtaining the property is not itself payload transmission.

rows.effect: Creates a writable stream that can send datagrams through its transport.
rows.prerequisites: Requires access to a usable native datagram duplex object and session.
rows.next: Test exposure in the target browser versions and receiver-observed writes; the pinned WPT case tests connection setup only.

rows.effect: Gets or sets incoming datagram expiration duration.
rows.prerequisites: Requires a reachable native datagram duplex object; setter validity and implementation support vary.
rows.next: Review effect on already queued datagrams and transmission timing. A property setter is not by itself proof that a peer receives data.

rows.effect: Gets or sets incoming datagram buffering limit.
rows.prerequisites: Requires a reachable native datagram duplex object; setter validity and implementation support vary.
rows.next: Review effect on already queued datagrams and transmission timing. A property setter is not by itself proof that a peer receives data.

rows.effect: Returns the maximum supported datagram size for the transport.
rows.prerequisites: Requires a reachable datagram duplex object and relevant connection state.
rows.next: Test actual datagram delivery through a separately acquired writable stream; reading this limit does not send a payload.

rows.effect: Gets or sets outgoing datagram expiration duration.
rows.prerequisites: Requires a reachable native datagram duplex object; setter validity and implementation support vary.
rows.next: Review effect on already queued datagrams and transmission timing. A property setter is not by itself proof that a peer receives data.

rows.effect: Gets or sets outgoing datagram buffering limit.
rows.prerequisites: Requires a reachable native datagram duplex object; setter validity and implementation support vary.
rows.next: Review effect on already queued datagrams and transmission timing. A property setter is not by itself proof that a peer receives data.

rows.effect: Returns the incoming datagram readable stream.
rows.prerequisites: Requires a reachable datagram duplex object and active session to receive data.
rows.next: Assess data provenance and other outbound capabilities separately.

rows.effect: Gets or sets the writable stream send group.
rows.prerequisites: Requires a reachable native writable stream; group assignment is constrained by its associated transport.
rows.next: Examine effects on scheduling of pending writes and any timing channels separately; assigning the property alone does not establish payload delivery.

rows.effect: Gets or sets the writable stream send order.

rows.next: Examine effects on scheduling of pending writes and any timing channels separately; assigning the property alone does not establish payload delivery.

rows.effect: Constructs a WebTransportError with supplied error information.
rows.prerequisites: Requires exposed API and valid initialization data.
rows.next: Trace how errors are used by actual stream/session operations; constructing an error object alone is not a network send.

rows.effect: Returns the transport error source.
rows.prerequisites: Requires an accessible WebTransportError, which may be synthetic or produced by a transport.
rows.next: Assess error provenance and separately test any relay or protocol control action.

rows.effect: Returns the transport error streamErrorCode.

rows.effect: Writes a chunk subject to atomic flow-control semantics; other errors can occur after partial delivery.
rows.prerequisites: Requires an accessible WebTransportWriter and a usable live stream; browser support for this writer is unknown.
rows.next: Calibrate actual partial and successful delivery against a receiver in relevant execution contexts.

rows.effect: Commits data on the writer according to the WebTransport writer algorithm.
rows.prerequisites: Requires an accessible native writer and applicable stream state; implementation support is unknown.
rows.next: Check precise buffering and transmission consequences against the current spec and receiver; do not assume it is a no-op or standalone upload.
